import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Define spending columns and their desired display names for the legend
spending_cols = {
    'MntWines': 'Wines',
    'MntMeatProducts': 'Meat',
    'MntGoldProds': 'Gold',
    'MntFishProducts': 'Fish',
    'MntSweetProducts': 'Sweets',
    'MntFruits': 'Fruits'
}

# Group by education and calculate the mean spending for each category
education_spending = df.groupby('Education')[list(spending_cols.keys())].mean()

# To make the comparison fair, calculate the proportion of spending on each category.
# This normalizes for the fact that some groups may have higher overall spending.
spending_proportions = education_spending.div(education_spending.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

# Define a logical order for education levels for the x-axis
education_order = ['Basic', 'Graduation', 'Master', '2n Cycle', 'PhD']
spending_proportions = spending_proportions.reindex(education_order)

# Reorder columns for a visually appealing stack (largest categories at the bottom)
col_order = ['MntWines', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntGoldProds', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntFruits']
spending_proportions = spending_proportions[col_order]


# --- Visualization ---

# Set plot style and create figure/axes
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Define a color palette for the product categories
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis_r", n_colors=len(spending_cols))

# Create the 100% stacked bar chart
spending_proportions.plot(
    kind='bar',
    stacked=True,
    color=colors,
    ax=ax,
    width=0.65,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# --- Customization and Labels ---

# Format Y-axis as percentage
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f'{y:.0%}'))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1) # Ensure y-axis goes from 0 to 100%

# Set titles and labels with appropriate font sizes
ax.set_title('Proportional Spending on Product Categories by Education Level', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Share of Total Spending', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Customize ticks for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center', fontsize=11)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Customize legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Use the clean display names for the legend
ax.legend(
    handles[::-1], # Reverse order to match stacking
    [spending_cols[label] for label in labels[::-1]],
    title='Product Category',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=10,
    title_fontsize=12
)

# Remove unnecessary spines for a cleaner look
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)

# Add a subtle horizontal grid and ensure it's behind the bars
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', visible=False)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# --- Save Figure ---
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
